I1.quote: Excess hydrogen adsorption measurements were performed on a 330 mg Basolite Z377 pellets sample using a volumetric Sieverts’ apparatus (PCT-Pro 2000 from Hy-Energy LLC) over the 0–50 bar and 50–120 K ranges.
I1.location: main, p. 2, Section 3.1 Volumetric adsorption measurements

I2.quote: Searched for any measured sorbent that is a carbon sorbent; none found. The only sorbent measured is Basolite Z377, 'actually the zinc-based Metal–Organic Framework, MOF-177' (p. 2, Section 2.1), pellets with <3 wt% graphite binder; AX-21 carbon values are 'literature data' (ref. 27).

I3.quote: at 3.5 MPa and 77 K, the hydrogen excess adsorption is about 43% higher on the MOF-177 pellets (50 mg g−1) than on the AX-21 pellets (35 mg g−1).
I3.location: main, p. 4, Section 4.2 Excess hydrogen adsorption isotherms

I4.quote: The densified MOF-177 has a specific surface area of about 2920 m2 g−1, a value about 26% less than the powder sample, which is about 3965 m2 g−1.
I4.location: main, p. 3, Section 4.1 Materials density and porosimetry (values also in Table 1, p. 4)

I5.quote: Exploring and evaluating on-board solid state hydrogen storage systems performance are of great interest for fuel cell electric vehicles development.

notes: Measured sorbent is MOF-177 (BASF Basolite Z377) pellets 'containing less than 3 wt% of graphite as a binder' (p. 2, Section 2.1); majority component is the MOF, so not a carbon sorbent under §3 (MOFs excluded).
